context: Invitation work broken into Jira TEAM tickets for parallel agents. A good plan cuts end-to-end behavior slices, blocks only where a ticket cannot start or be verified without another, and says what can start now. Topic overlap or a preferred order is not a blocking edge.

checklist.name: Only necessary blocking edges
checklist.description: Accept and revoke are each blocked by the ticket that creates invitations, and revoke is not blocked by accept. No edge exists only for topic overlap or a preferred order.

checklist.name: Vertical slices
checklist.description: Each ticket delivers an end-to-end behavior (UI, API, storage, and tests together). There is no separate UI, API, database, data-model, foundation, or test ticket.

checklist.name: Frontier stated
checklist.description: The answer states that only invitation creation can start now and that accept and revoke can run in parallel once it lands.

checklist.name: Epic with children
checklist.description: One TEAM epic parents the tickets, and the links use Jira parent and blocks relationships.

checklist.name: Each ticket verifiable
checklist.description: Each ticket names its own acceptance or proof of the delivered behavior.

checklist.name: No implementation or local backlog
checklist.description: No source code is written and no plan or backlog file is created in the repository.
